import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import os
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.ensemble import RandomForestClassifier
from sklearn.preprocessing import LabelEncoder
from sklearn.metrics import log_loss

# Ensure submission directory exists
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

# Load data
train_df = pd.read_csv("./input/train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv("./input/test.csv")
sample_sub = pd.read_csv("./input/sample_submission.csv")

# Identify feature columns
# Features are margin1-64, shape1-64, texture1-64
# Excluding 'id' and 'species'
feature_cols = [col for col in train_df.columns if col not in ["id", "species"]]

X = train_df[feature_cols]
y = train_df["species"]
X_test = test_df[feature_cols]
test_ids = test_df["id"]

# Encode labels to integers to ensure log_loss compatibility with predict_proba columns
le = LabelEncoder()
y_encoded = le.fit_transform(y)
y_classes = le.classes_  # This should match model.classes_ (sorted)

# Stratified split
X_train, X_val, y_train_enc, y_val_enc = train_test_split(
    X, y_encoded, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_encoded
)

# Train Random Forest
# Using a simple configuration without hyperparameter tuning
model = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1)
model.fit(X_train, y_train_enc)

# Evaluate on validation set
val_pred_proba = model.predict_proba(X_val)
# log_loss expects y_true integers and y_pred probabilities in class order
val_score = log_loss(y_val_enc, val_pred_proba)
print(f"Validation Multi-class Log Loss: {val_score}")

# Train on full data for submission
model_full = RandomForestClassifier(n_estimators=100, random_state=42, n_jobs=1)
model_full.fit(X, y_encoded)

# Predict on test set
test_pred_proba = model_full.predict_proba(X_test)

# Prepare submission
# Create dataframe with probabilities
# Columns should be the species names
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(test_pred_proba, columns=model_full.classes_)

# Reorder columns to match sample_submission (excluding 'id')
submission_cols = sample_sub.columns[1:]
# Ensure all submission columns are present in model classes
# model_full.classes_ should contain all species
submission_df = submission_df[submission_cols]

# Add id column
submission_df.insert(0, "id", test_ids)

# Save submission
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print("Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")
